label: Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center
other synonyms: Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center|Knight ADRC Memory and Aging Project
example title: Identification of genetic modifiers of autosomal dominant Alzheimer's disease: a genome-wide association study.
example quote: In this genome-wide association study (GWAS), we analysed data from individuals carrying ADAD mutations and control participants from three cohorts— the Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center (Knight-ADRC),18 the Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) observational study, and the Alzheimer Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP) R4.
definition: A cohort of research volunteers recruited over more than 40 years by the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center at Washington University in St. Louis, United States, largely through its Memory and Aging Project and Memory Diagnostic Clinic, and followed with cognitive, neuropsychological, imaging, fluid biomarker, genomic and multi-omic assessments to study Alzheimer disease and related dementias.
location quote: The Knight-Alzheimer Disease Research Center (Knight-ADRC) at Washington University in St. Louis has pioneered and led worldwide seminal studies that have expanded our clinical, social, pathological, and molecular understanding of Alzheimer Disease.
note: Not in COHO under any name. Tags Knight_ADRC and Knight-ADRC (~30,457 GCSTs, 7 PMIDs, mostly CSF/plasma pQTL and metabolite QTL studies) are one cohort; row Knight-ADRC is the duplicate. The pQTL papers call it the Knight ADRC Memory and Aging Project (MAP) and split it into Knight-ADRC (Oct 2021) and (June 2023) proteomic batches. Country inferred from St. Louis (Missouri). Knight-ADRC participants carrying ADAD mutations are referred to DIAN (PMID:38997326), so the two samples can overlap. Example study PMID:42127933 also carries tags DIAN and ADSP.

input name: Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
label: Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center
note: Duplicate of Knight_ADRC (same GWAS tags, same center; PGS names differ only by the donors' names); see row Knight_ADRC.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
example title: Genome-Wide association study of quantitative biomarkers identifies a novel locus for alzheimer's disease at 12p12.1.
example quote: Data used in this analysis was obtained from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database [47].
definition: A multi-site longitudinal cohort of cognitively normal older adults and people with mild cognitive impairment or mild Alzheimer disease, recruited from 2004 at over 60 clinical sites in the United States and Canada by the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, a public-private partnership, to evaluate neuroimaging, fluid biomarker and clinical measures of Alzheimer disease progression.
location quote: Researchers at over 60 clinical sites in the USA and Canada collect data to study the progression of AD in the human brain across normal aging, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer’s disease and dementia.
note: Not in COHO. Tag ADNI: 13,746 GCSTs, 31 PMIDs; example is a single-cohort ADNI GWAS (PMID:35086473). ADNI phases (ADNI 1/GO/2/3/4) are not separate tags here; ADNI-DOD is a separate tag outside this batch. The GWAS-tagged ADNI studies also include sub-studies such as ADNI CSF pQTL samples.

label: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network
example title: Identification of genetic modifiers of autosomal dominant Alzheimer's disease: a genome-wide association study.
example quote: In this genome-wide association study (GWAS), we analysed data from individuals carrying ADAD mutations and control participants from three cohorts— the Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center (Knight-ADRC),18 the Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) observational study, and the Alzheimer Disease Sequencing Project (ADSP) R4.
definition: An international longitudinal cohort of asymptomatic and symptomatic carriers of autosomal dominant Alzheimer disease mutations and their non-carrier family members, followed by a network of Alzheimer disease centres coordinated from Washington University in St. Louis with standard clinical, cognitive, neuroimaging and fluid biomarker protocols to determine the pathochronology of the disease.
location quote: Washington University (St. Louis, Missouri, USA) is the coordinating center for DIAN, which has 11 current performance sites in the US, United Kingdom, and Australia.
note: Not in COHO. Tag DIAN: 12,791 GCSTs, 7 PMIDs. Label drops the PGS name's leading "The". Countries are those of the 2012 description; the 2013 review (PMC3978584) already lists sites in Tubingen and Munich, Germany, and DIAN has since expanded further - curator may add Germany and later countries. The DIAN observational study is distinct from the DIAN Trials Unit (DIAN-TU).

label: Barcelona-1
other synonyms: Longitudinal observational study from the Memory and Disorder unit at the University Hospital Mutua de Terrassa
example title: Proteogenomic analysis of human cerebrospinal fluid identifies neurologically relevant regulation and implicates causal proteins for Alzheimer's disease.
example quote: Genomic datasets from ADNI, DIAN, Knight-ADRC (Oct 2021), Knight-ADRC (June 2023), MARS, FACE, and Barcelona-1 were genotyped on multiple arrays at different times and were imputed individually using the GRCh38 Version R2 reference panel on the TOPMed imputation server.
definition: A longitudinal observational memory-clinic cohort of about 300 people at baseline, diagnosed with Alzheimer disease dementia, other dementias, mild cognitive impairment or subjective memory complaints, assembled at the Memory Disorders Unit of the University Hospital Mútua de Terrassa near Barcelona, Spain, with cerebrospinal fluid and amyloid PET biomarkers collected for selected participants.
location quote: Barcelona -1 is a longitudinal observational study consisting of ~300 subjects at baseline carried out in the Memory and Disorder unit at the University Hospital Mutua de Terrassa, Terrassa, Barcelona, Spain.
note: Not in COHO. Tag Barcelona-1: 12,786 GCSTs, 5 PMIDs, mostly Cruchaga-lab CSF pQTL/metabolite studies. The cohort has no longer formal name in the sources read, so the label is the study's own name. Doubt: the tag is also on PMID:39132902 (levodopa-induced dyskinesia GWAS in Parkinson disease, GCST90281037/GCST90281038); I could not read that paper's cohort description (only a fragment of the full text was available), so whether Barcelona-1 there is this memory-clinic cohort or a Barcelona Parkinson cohort is unverified.

Placeholder ("Unknown or unspecified cohort") used by the PGS Catalog and by the GWAS Catalog tags OTHER/Other/other (11,958 GCSTs) for cohorts that were not named or not in the curation list; not a cohort.

input name: Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Networks Engineering Task
label: Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Networks Engineering Task
other synonyms: Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Engineering Task
example title: Deciphering tissue-specific protein regulation for insights into cardiometabolic disease.
example quote: Utilizing Olink technology, we assessed relative protein levels across plasma and tissue (aortic wall, mammary artery, liver, and skeletal muscle) from the STARNET cohort: 284 individuals with a high prevalence of coronary artery disease (CAD).
definition: A cohort of patients with coronary artery disease undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting, with comparison patients undergoing other open-heart surgery, enrolled at the Department of Cardiac Surgery of Tartu University Hospital in Estonia, whose vascular and metabolic tissues and blood were genotyped, RNA-sequenced and proteomically profiled to study gene regulation underlying cardiometabolic disease.
location quote: Coronary artery disease (CAD) patients eligible for coronary artery by-pass grafting (CABG) surgery (n = 200) and controls eligible for other open-heart surgeries (e.g. valve replacement, n = 84), verified to be CAD-free in pre-operative coronary angiograms, were enrolled at the Department of Cardiac Surgery, Tartu University Hospital.
note: Not in COHO. Tag STARNET: 11,432 GCSTs, all from PMID:41456820 (tissue/plasma pQTLs). Label as in the design paper PMID:27540175 (600 CAD patients); PMID:41456820 spells it without "Networks", kept as a synonym. Recruitment in Tartu (the same URL gives the affiliation Tartu University, Tartu, Estonia); "Stockholm" reflects the Karolinska analysis partner, not a recruitment site.
Placeholder "Not Reported" (tag NR, 9,508 GCSTs); not a cohort.

label: Million Veteran Program
other synonyms: VA Million Veteran Program
example title: Diversity and scale: Genetic architecture of 2068 traits in the VA Million Veteran Program.
example quote: We present genome-wide associations for 2068 traits from 635,969 participants in the Department of Veterans Affairs Million Veteran Program, a longitudinal study of diverse United States Veterans.
definition: An observational cohort and mega-biobank of veterans enrolled since 2011 at recruiting sites of the Department of Veterans Affairs health care system in the United States, combining questionnaires, electronic health records and blood samples for genomic testing to study genetic influences on health and disease.
location quote: We present genome-wide associations for 2068 traits from 635,969 participants in the Department of Veterans Affairs Million Veteran Program, a longitudinal study of diverse United States Veterans.
note: 8080 GWAS Catalog studies tagged MVP (101 PMIDs); no COHO match for MVP/Million Veteran/veteran; MVP has no acronym clash in COHO. Definition from the MVP design paper abstract (Gaziano et al. 2016).

label: Chinese Imaging Genetics study
other synonyms: Chinese Imaging Genetics|Chinese Imaging Genetics cohort
example title: Genome-wide association study of hippocampal blood-oxygen-level-dependent-cerebral blood flow correlation in Chinese Han population.
example quote: In this study, we conducted the first GWAS on the hippocampal BOLD-CBF correlation in 4,832 Chinese Han participants from the Chinese Imaging Genetics (CHIMGEN) cohort.22 Here, the across-voxel correlation between reginal homogeneity (ReHo) derived from the resting-state fMRI data and CBF measured by the arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI data within hippocampal voxels was used as a proxy to represent hippocampal NVC.
definition: A cohort of healthy Chinese Han adults aged 18–30 years recruited at research centres in mainland Chinese cities by the Chinese Imaging Genetics (CHIMGEN) study, collecting genomic, neuroimaging, environmental and behavioural data to identify genetic and environmental factors associated with neuroimaging and behavioural phenotypes.
location quote: The aim of this study was to collect genomic, neuroimaging, environmental, and behavioral data from 10,000 healthy Chinese Han participants aged 18–30 years in 30 research centers from 21 mainland cities in China.
note: 7045 GWAS Catalog studies tagged CHIMGEN (4 PMIDs, all single-tag); label from the profile paper (PMID:31827248, which calls it "the Chinese Imaging Genetics (CHIMGEN) study"). The example quote sentence ends with a citation marker "22" glued to the full stop, as printed in the full text.

input name: African American Study of Kidney disease and hypertension
label: African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension
other synonyms: AASK Cohort Study
example title: Identification of 969 protein quantitative trait loci in an African American population with kidney disease attributed to hypertension.
example quote: Here, we report the genetic determinants of the serum proteome in 466 African Americans with chronic kidney disease attributed to hypertension from the richly phenotyped African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension (AASK) study.
definition: A cohort of African American adults aged 18–70 with hypertensive chronic kidney disease, enrolled at clinical centres across the United States in a randomized trial of antihypertensive drug regimens and blood-pressure goals (1995–2001) and then followed in the AASK Cohort Study to identify risk factors for progressive kidney disease.
location quote: The African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension (AASK) was conducted over a 7-year period at 21 clinical centers across the United States to investigate whether one of two levels of blood pressure control and/or one of three classes of antihypertensive medications was more effective at slowing the rate of renal disease in African Americans with renal insufficiency presumed secondary to hypertension.
note: 6790 GWAS Catalog studies tagged AASK, all from one pQTL paper (PMID:35870639). PGS name lower-cases "Disease"; label uses the literature capitalisation. Began as a clinical trial, continued as the AASK Cohort Study; one term suggested for both.

label: UK Biobank
example title: A metabolomic profile of biological aging in 250,341 individuals from the UK Biobank.
example quote: Here, we analyse 325 nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) biomarkers from 250,341 UK Biobank participants, identifying 54 representative aging-related biomarkers associated with all-cause mortality.
note: GWAS-only tag: 5547 studies, 9 PMIDs; all 9 titles/abstracts checked name UK Biobank (incl. Pan-UK Biobank, PMID:40968291). COHO:0000176 has synonym UKB but not UKBB; UKBB clashes with nothing (UKBEC COHO:0000177 and UKBS COHO:0000347 are different strings).

label: Amsterdam Dementia Cohort
example title: Quantitative trait loci mapping of circulating metabolites in cerebrospinal fluid to uncover biological mechanisms involved in brain-related phenotypes.
example quote: Individuals originated from two separate cohorts including cognitively healthy subjects (n = 490) and a well-characterized memory clinic sample, the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort (ADC, n = 487).
definition: A cohort of almost 6,000 patients who have visited the memory clinic of the Alzheimer Center at VU University Medical Center (Amsterdam UMC) in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, since 2000, followed in an ongoing observational study that combines patient care with research on early diagnosis, heterogeneity and vascular factors in dementia.
location quote: The ADC started collecting samples in the year 2000 and is an ongoing, observational follow-up study of patients who visited the memory clinic of the Alzheimer Center at Amsterdam UMC, location VU University medical center (VUmc).
note: Not in COHO. Tag AmDem: 5,546 GCSTs, 2 PMIDs (CSF metabolite QTLs PMID:40021830; ADRD meta-analysis PMID:42237039). The cohort's own acronym is ADC (no clash in COHO). Country inferred from Amsterdam. In PMID:40021830 the memory-clinic sample also includes the related 90+ Study and Twin Study, all tagged AmDem.

label: Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits Study
other synonyms: Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits in Parkinson Disease
example title: Low overlap of plasma and CSF protein quantitative trait loci affects protein discovery for neurological disease.
definition: A longitudinal cohort of people with Parkinson disease and healthy older controls studied by the Campbell Research Lab in the Section of Movement Disorders at Washington University in St. Louis, United States, assessed every two years with MRI, motor, gait and cognitive testing, optional lumbar puncture and clinical interview to understand the role of brain proteins and neurotransmitters in Parkinson disease symptoms compared with healthy aging.
location quote: Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits (PAND) Study | Campbell Research Lab | Washington University in St. Louis
note: Not in COHO. Tag PAND: 5,330 GCSTs, all from PMID:42054495 (plasma vs CSF pQTLs; Science Translational Medicine, not open access, no preprint found), so no example quote could be verified; the study list comes from the GWAS Catalog record (cohort field of GCST90939806). Identified from the WashU Campbell lab study page (PGS name matches); the NIH IADRP project title is "Protein aggregation and neurotransmitter deficits in Parkinson disease". Location quote is the page title; country inferred from St. Louis. Not a Knight ADRC sub-study as far as sources show. Follow-up 2026-09-23: Europe PMC full-text search for "Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits" (3 hits: PMC12991935, an unrelated mouse study; PMC11590651 and PMC6260199, not open access and their text not retrievable) and for "Neurotransmitter Deficits" AND Parkinson AND "Washington University" (9 hits, none naming the study in open text) found no open-access text naming the cohort, so there is still no example quote. Verified definition-source text from the lab page: "The purpose of this study is to understand the role of brain proteins and neurotransmitters in the symptoms of PD compared to healthy aging."

label: Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson Disease Study
example title: Low overlap of plasma and CSF protein quantitative trait loci affects protein discovery for neurological disease.
definition: A longitudinal cohort of people with Parkinson disease and healthy older controls studied by the Campbell Research Lab in the Section of Movement Disorders at Washington University in St. Louis, United States, assessed every three years with MRI, motor, gait and cognitive testing, optional lumbar puncture, amyloid and cholinergic PET and clinical interview to relate clinical symptoms to brain changes in Parkinson disease compared with healthy aging.
location quote: Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson Disease (PIB) Study | Campbell Research Lab | Washington University in St. Louis
note: PIB is a cohort name, not Pittsburgh compound B: it is the WashU Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson Disease (PIB) Study (whose protocol includes amyloid PET, hence the acronym overlap). Tag PIB: 5,330 GCSTs, all from PMID:42054495 (not open access), listed with PAND and other WashU/Knight cohorts in the GWAS Catalog cohort field of GCST90939806; no example quote could be verified. The PGS id PIB (name "PIB") comes from PGS000777 (PMID:33958783, Liu et al. 2021), whose open text lists "PIB" among 15 Parkinson progression cohorts without expanding it; J.S. Perlmutter (WashU) is an author, so it is probably the same WashU study but this is unverified - curator should check that paper's Supplementary Table 1. Location quote is the page title; country inferred from St. Louis. Follow-up 2026-09-23: Europe PMC full-text searches ("Protein and Imaging Biomarkers" AND Parkinson: 4 hits; "Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson": 1 hit) found one open-access paper naming the cohort, PMID:33213513 (PMC7678051; not in the GWAS Catalog table, so not usable as the example study): "The discovery phase included 729 individuals from the Protein and Imaging Biomarkers in Parkinson’s disease study (PIB-PD) at the Washington University Movement Disorder Center [9] (n = 103) and the Knight ADRC [24] (n = 626)." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7678051/fullTextXML); PIB-PD added as an acronym. Verified definition-source text from the lab page: "The purpose of this study is to understand the relationship between clinical symptoms and brain changes in people with PD as compared to healthy aging." The PGS paper PMID:33958783 (PMC8459648, BioC) lists "PIB" among its discovery cohorts without expanding it, so the identity of the PGS PIB with this study remains unconfirmed. The example study still has no quote (PMID:42054495 is not open access).

label: BioBank Japan
other synonyms: BioBank Japan Project
example title: Pan-cancer and cross-population genome-wide association studies dissect shared genetic backgrounds underlying carcinogenesis.
example quote: Here, we conduct the pan-cancer and cross-population genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis and replication studies on 13 cancers including 250,015 East Asians (Biobank Japan) and 377,441 Europeans (UK Biobank).
definition: A patient-based biobank of about 200,000 people diagnosed with any of 47 common diseases, enrolled in 2003–2008 at 12 cooperative medical institutes across Japan by the BioBank Japan Project, with DNA, serum and annually collected clinical information to support genomic research and personalized medicine.
location quote: Patients were enrolled at 12 cooperative medical institutes all over Japan from June 2003 to March 2008.
note: 5082 GWAS Catalog studies tagged BBJ (96 PMIDs). Label "BioBank Japan" as the profile paper uses it for the biobank; the PGS name "BioBank Japan Project" (the project that built it) kept as synonym. No COHO match for BBJ/BioBank Japan. Example abstract spells it "Biobank Japan".

label: INTERVAL study
example title: A genome-wide association study of blood cell morphology identifies cellular proteins implicated in disease aetiology.
example quote: We perform genome-wide association studies of 63 flow-cytometry derived cellular phenotypes-including cell-type specific measures of granularity, nucleic acid content and reactivity-in 41,515 participants in the INTERVAL study.
note: 5068 GWAS Catalog studies tagged INTERVAL (20 PMIDs; abstracts checked name the INTERVAL study of blood donors). COHO:0000184 has label "INTERVAL study" and no synonym INTERVAL, so INTERVAL is proposed as an acronym synonym; no clash.

label: Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study
other synonyms: Aging Gene-Environment Susceptibility - Reykjavik Study
example title: A genome-wide association study of serum proteins reveals shared loci with common diseases.
example quote: We performed a GWAS of 4782 serum proteins encoded by 4135 unique human genes in the population-based AGES cohort of elderly Icelanders (n = 5368, Supplementary Data 1), measured by the slow-off rate modified aptamer (SOMAmer) platform as previously described8,18.
definition: A cohort of older men and women born in 1907–1935, drawn from the population-based Reykjavik Study followed in Iceland by the Icelandic Heart Association and re-examined from 2002 with detailed cardiovascular, neurocognitive, musculoskeletal and metabolic phenotypes to study genetic susceptibility and gene–environment interaction in disease and disability in old age.
location quote: This cohort of men and women born between 1907 and 1935 has been followed in Iceland since 1967 by the Icelandic Heart Association.
parent quote: The AGES-Reykjavik sample is drawn from an established population-based cohort, the Reykjavik Study.
note: 4917 GWAS Catalog studies tagged AGES (13 PMIDs). PGS name "Aging Gene-Environment Susceptibility" is a garbled form; label follows the design paper (Harris et al. 2007). Sub-cohort of the Reykjavik Study (not in COHO): "The AGES-Reykjavik sample is drawn from an established population-based cohort, the Reykjavik Study." (PMID:17351290 abstract), so parent left empty. No COHO match or clash for AGES/Reykjavik. Parent (Reykjavik Study, a new row of this review) added on 2026-09-23.

label: Stanford Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
other synonyms: Stanford Iqbal Farrukh and Asad Jamal ADRC
example title: Proteo-genomics of soluble TREM2 in cerebrospinal fluid provides novel insights and identifies novel modulators for Alzheimer's disease.
example quote: Stanford Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (ADRC) (https://med.stanford.edu/adrc.html), one of thirty-one ADRC, aims to translate research advances into improved diagnosis and care for people with AD and related disorders.
definition: A cohort of research participants followed by the Stanford Alzheimer's Disease Research Center, one of the US National Institutes of Health-funded Alzheimer's Disease Research Centers, whose clinical and research focus spans Alzheimer disease and Lewy body disorders, contributing cerebrospinal fluid proteomic and whole-genome sequence data to genetic studies.
location quote: The Stanford Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (ADRC) is part of a nationwide network of congressionally mandated Centers of Excellence supported by the National Institutes of Health.
note: Not in COHO. Tag Stanford_ADRC: 4,649 GCSTs, 2 PMIDs. In PMID:39528825 the tag covers "Stanford Iqbal Farrukh and Asad Jamal ADRC & Aging Memory Study [Stanford]", i.e. the ADRC plus the Stanford Aging and Memory Study (SAMS), which a curator may want as a separate cohort. Country inferred from the NIH nationwide-network statement and Stanford, CA (no explicit country in the quote).

label: Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging
example title: Effect modification by sex of genetic associations of vitamin C related metabolites in the Canadian Longitudinal study on aging.
example quote: Methods: We included individuals of European descent from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging with available genetic and metabolic data (n = 9004).
definition: A national stratified cohort of 51,338 women and men aged 45–85 years recruited in 2011–2015 from all 10 Canadian provinces, comprising a telephone-interviewed Tracking cohort and an in-person Comprehensive cohort providing physical assessments and blood and urine samples, assembled as a longitudinal research platform for studying health and aging.
location quote: In the Tracking cohort, participants were recruited across the 10 provinces, and all questionnaire measures are collected by computer-assisted telephone interviews (CATI) administered through CLSA CATI sites established in four regions across Canada to accommodate different time zones and language (English or French) requirements for questionnaire administration.
note: 4461 GWAS Catalog studies tagged CLSA (10 PMIDs). Definition from the cohort profile (Raina et al. 2019, PMC6929533 full text). No COHO match or clash.

label: Jackson Heart Study
example title: Whole Genome Association Study of the Plasma Metabolome Identifies Metabolites Linked to Cardiometabolic Disease in Black Individuals.
example quote: Here, we perform a whole genome association study of 2,291 metabolite peaks (known and unknown features) in 2,466 Black individuals from the Jackson Heart Study.
definition: A community-based cohort of 5,302 African American adults, including a nested family cohort, enrolled from the three counties of the Jackson, Mississippi metropolitan area, with extensive medical, social, physical and biochemical measurements and genomic DNA, to study cardiovascular and related diseases in African Americans.
location quote: Participants were enrolled from the three counties that make up the Jackson, Mississippi metropolitan area.
note: 3953 GWAS Catalog studies tagged JHS (42 PMIDs). Location quote names Jackson, Mississippi (a US state), not the country itself; it is a substring of the abstract, which Europe PMC prints glued to its "Methods" heading. No COHO match or clash.

label: UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project
other synonyms: UK Biobank Pharma Plasma Proteome|UKB Pharma Plasma Proteome|Pharma Proteomics Project
example title: Rare variant associations with plasma protein levels in the UK Biobank.
example quote: The UKB Pharma Plasma Proteome (UKB-PPP) cohort comprises plasma samples from 54,219 individuals, including 46,595 randomly selected participants, 6,376 consortium-chosen individuals and 1,268 participants from a COVID-19 repeat imaging study.
definition: A sub-cohort of 54,219 UK Biobank participants, mostly a random selection of baseline participants plus individuals chosen by consortium members and participants in the COVID-19 repeat-imaging study, whose plasma proteomes were profiled by the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project, a precompetitive consortium of biopharmaceutical companies, to map genetic and health associations of circulating proteins.
parent quote: The Pharma Proteomics Project is a precompetitive biopharmaceutical consortium characterizing the plasma proteomic profiles of 54,219 UK Biobank participants.
note: 2941 GWAS Catalog studies tagged UKB-PPP, all from PMID:37794183. Label from the flagship paper (Sun et al. 2023, PMC10567551: "we formed the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP)"); the PGS name "Pharma Plasma Proteome" is the form used in the ExWAS paper and kept as synonym. Country asserted from the parent UK Biobank / the name, without a quote. No COHO clash.

label: Mass General Brigham Biobank
other synonyms: MGB Biobank|Partners Biobank
example title: Genetics and context for precision health in Greater Boston.
example quote: We established the Mass General Brigham Biobank (MGBB), currently encompassing 142,238 participants, to unravel the intricate relationships among genomic profiles, environmental context, and disease manifestations within clinical practice.
definition: A healthcare-based biobank of more than 140,000 consenting patients of the Mass General Brigham network in the Greater Boston area of Massachusetts, enrolled since 2010 at Massachusetts General Hospital, Brigham and Women’s Hospital and local sites, linking biological samples, genomic data and health records to study genetic and environmental influences on disease in clinical practice.
location quote: Mass General Brigham, an integrated healthcare system based in the Greater Boston area of Massachusetts, annually serves 1.5 million patients.
note: 2319 GWAS Catalog studies tagged MGBB (35 PMIDs). Former name from the full text (PMC12749686): "MGBB, previously known as Partners Biobank, is an integrated research initiative based in Boston, Massachusetts." The PGS table also has PHB "Partners HealthCare Biobank", the same biobank under its former name (now a row of this review, see below); a curator should merge it here. Location quote names Massachusetts, not the country. No COHO match or clash. Follow-up 2026-09-23: the PGS cohort PHB (Partners HealthCare Biobank) is added at the end of the file with same as = MGBB, so PHB and "Partners HealthCare Biobank" become synonyms of this term.

label: Cardiovascular Health Study
example title: Circulating Soluble CD163, Associations With Cardiovascular Outcomes and Mortality, and Identification of Genetic Variants in Older Individuals: The Cardiovascular Health Study.
example quote: Methods and Results We measured plasma sCD163 in 5214 adults (aged ≥65 years, 58.7% women, 16.2% Black) of the CHS (Cardiovascular Health Study).
definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of men and women aged 65 years and older sampled from Medicare eligibility lists in four US communities (Forsyth County, North Carolina; Sacramento County, California; Washington County, Maryland; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania) from 1989, with mostly Black participants added in 1992–1993, to identify factors related to the onset and course of coronary heart disease and stroke in older adults.
location quote: The study design called for enrollment of 1250 men and women in each of four communities: Forsyth County, North Carolina;
note: 2166 GWAS Catalog studies tagged CHS (57 PMIDs); titles scanned are all adult cardiovascular/TOPMed/CHARGE-type studies, no sign of the Childrens Health Study (PGS CHS_b) using this tag, but not every paper was opened. Location quote names US states, not the country. No COHO match or clash (CHS_b is a different PGS id, not in COHO).

label: Framingham Heart Study
example title: A Genome-Wide Interaction Study of Erythrocyte ω-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid Species and Memory in the Framingham Heart Study Offspring Cohort.
example quote: The Offspring cohort from the Framingham Heart Study was cross-sectionally analyzed in this genome-wide interaction study (GWIS).
definition: A community-based, multi-generational cohort of residents of Framingham, Massachusetts, begun with the Original Cohort in 1948 and extended by the Offspring (1971), Third Generation (2002) and OMNI cohorts, examined every 2–4 years to define cardiovascular disease risk factors and, increasingly, the genetic and molecular epidemiology of a wide range of diseases.
location quote: Framingham Heart Study, which is a longitudinal, multi-generational community-based cohort based in Framingham, Massachusetts, USA.
note: 2151 GWAS Catalog studies tagged FHS (63 PMIDs); abstracts matching FHS all mean Framingham; no sign of the British Heart Foundation Family Heart Study (PGS BHF-FHS) using this tag. Quotes are substrings of structured abstracts that Europe PMC prints glued to their headings ("Methods", "Setting"). FHS comprises several generational cohorts (Original, Offspring, Third Generation, OMNI) that a curator may later want as sub-cohorts. No COHO match or clash.

label: Rhineland Study
example title: Population-based genome-wide association study of plasma complex lipid species.
example quote: Thus, we perform genome-wide association studies on 970 lipid species and 267 fatty acid composite measures using samples from the population-based Rhineland Study (n = 6096).
definition: An ongoing population-based cohort of people aged 30 or above living in two geographically defined areas of Bonn, Germany, invited in random order by the German Centre for Neurodegenerative Diseases (DZNE) for deep phenotyping, imaging and omics studies of health and ageing.
location quote: We used data from the Rhineland Study, an ongoing population-based cohort study in Bonn, Germany, to perform a GWAS on circulating complex lipid levels and composition measured using the Metabolon Complex Lipids Platform.
note: 2094 GWAS Catalog studies over 5 PMIDs (1826 from PMID:42069741). Definition from the methods of PMC13135507 (People aged 30 or above who lived in either of two geographically defined areas in Bonn were invited to participate.); DZNE affiliation from the same paper's author list. No design paper found in Europe PMC by title search. Label as the study calls itself (Rhineland Study); PGS name 'The Rhineland Study'.

input name: European Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition, Potsdam study

example title: Extending the use of GWAS data by combining data from different genetic platforms.
example quote: We included a total of 979 unique patients from the previously described prospective cohort AMC-PAS[6], with symptomatic Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) before the age of 51 years, defined as Myocardial Infarction (MI), coronary revascularization, or evidence of at least 70% stenosis in a major epicardial artery.
definition: A prospective cohort of patients of the Academic Medical Center, Amsterdam, with symptomatic coronary artery disease (myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization or at least 70% stenosis of a major epicardial artery) before the age of 51, used in genetic studies of premature atherosclerosis and coronary artery disease.
location quote: PAS, Premature Atherosclerosis Study—Academic Medical Center—Amsterdam;
parent quote: Over the last two years pedigree histories have been compiled from the AMC-PAS cohort and so far ten families have been identified with evidence of autosomal inheritance of CVD without any known monogenic causes of CVD.
note: The evidence supports the Amsterdam reading, not the PGS name: the PGS full name "Osteoporosis Clinic of Asan Medical Center" is wrong. All 8 PGS uses (PGS000011/12/18/20/58/349/818/877) are CAD, T2D or insulin-resistance scores built on CARDIoGRAMplusC4D/DIAGRAM-type meta-analyses, and those consortia expand AMC-PAS as "Academic Medical Center Amsterdam Premature Atherosclerosis Study" (PMC5525436). COHO:0000322 "Premature Atherosclerosis Study pedigrees" is a different, smaller collection: its EGA study (EGAS00001000052) says pedigree histories "have been compiled from the AMC-PAS cohort" (ten families). So COHO's synonym AMC-PAS on COHO:0000322 looks wrong: it names the parent cohort. Suggest moving AMC-PAS to this new term and making COHO:0000322 isSubCohortOf it. The alternative is to relabel COHO:0000322 as the whole AMC-PAS cohort. Location comes from the cohort's name (Academic Medical Center, Amsterdam), not from a recruitment statement. No GWAS Catalog tag found (no AMC/PAS tags); the example is a non-PGS paper using the cohort, since the PGS publications' texts gave no quotable AMC-PAS sentence. Follow-up 2026-09-23: the parent quote and URL are for the CHILD link, not a parent of this row: COHO:0000322 (Premature Atherosclerosis Study pedigrees, EGA study EGAS00001000052) is to become isSubCohortOf this new term, and keeps AMC-PAS as its own synonym (the EGA tag); both terms then carry AMC-PAS and each gets an editor note. This supersedes the suggestion above to move the synonym.

label: Bogalusa Heart Study
example title: Genome-wide association studies identify 137 genetic loci for DNA methylation biomarkers of aging.
example quote: The BHS is a long-term epidemiology study of the natural history of cardiovascular disease from childhood to adulthood in the community of Bogalusa (65% white, 35% African American), Louisiana, the United States
definition: A long-term community-based cohort of Black and white children and adolescents in the rural biracial community of Bogalusa, Louisiana, United States, begun in 1972 by an NHLBI-funded research centre to study cardiovascular risk factors from early life and followed into adulthood.
location quote: Bogalusa, LA, is a biracial (black/white) rural community 70 miles north of New Orleans, comparable to many other communities in southeastern United States.
note: GWAS tag BHS is shared: the 18 GWAS Catalog studies (24 cohort-table lines) of PMID:34187551 are Bogalusa (Additional file 1 of that paper, 13059_2021_2398_MOESM1_ESM.docx in the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles bundle, describes "Bogalusa Heart Study (BHS)"; the example quote is from that file, the article text does not name the cohort); the 1868 studies of PMID:35668104 and 9 of PMID:36914875 are Busselton. Acronym BHS clashes with review row BHS (Busselton Health Study, not yet in COHO); curator to add editor notes to both. PGS Catalog also lists BHS as another name of Baependi (Baependi Heart Study). No COHO term matches BHS, BHS_b or Bogalusa (coho.sh). PGS BHS_b: 12 evaluation PGS.

input name: Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study
label: Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study
example title: Association between genes regulating neural pathways for quantitative traits of speech and language disorders.
example quote: We conducted a GWAS in the Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study (CFSRS), a cohort ascertained through a proband with SSD, and replicated findings in a population-based cohort.
definition: A family-based longitudinal cohort of children with speech sound disorder of unknown cause and their siblings, ascertained through probands referred by speech-language pathologists in the Cleveland area of Ohio, United States, and followed for about 25 years to study long-term speech, language and literacy outcomes and their genetic basis.
location quote: Children with a diagnosis of SSD were referred to the study from the clinical caseloads of SLPs in Ohio.
note: The literature (PMID:34315907, the 2025 review PMID:41118674) uses the acronym CFSRS, never CFS; CFS kept only because it is the GWAS tag. GWAS tag CFS misused: only the 16 studies of PMID:34315907 are this cohort; all other CFS-tagged studies (22 other PMIDs) are the Cleveland Family Study (sleep apnoea). Acronym CFS clashes with review row CFS (Cleveland Family Study, not yet in COHO); curator to add editor notes to both. No COHO term matches CFS, CFSRS or Cleveland (coho.sh). Location quote names Ohio (a US state), not the country.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium
example title: Multi-trait genome-wide association study of opioid addiction: OPRM1 and beyond.
example quote: We applied genomic structural equation modeling to conduct a GWAS of the new Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium (GENOA) data together with published studies (Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, Million Veteran Program, and Partners Health), comprising 23,367 cases and effective sample size of 88,114 individuals of European ancestry.
definition: A consortium of investigators attending the National Institute on Drug Abuse Genetics and Epigenetics Cross-cutting Research Team meetings, pooling genome-wide association data on opioid addiction from ten independent cohorts, including Yale-Penn, the Vancouver Injection Drug Users Study, the Urban Health Study, COGA, deCODE and the Comorbidity and Trauma Study, to study the genetics of opioid addiction.
note: Consortium, not a cohort: "GENOA is a new consortium comprised of investigators who attend the National Institute on Drug Abuse Genetics and Epigenetics Cross-cutting Research Team Meetings and who have GWAS data on OA (Supplementary Table 1)." (PMC9546890 full text). Members (Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary Fig. 9 legend): Yale-Penn-CIDR, Yale-Penn-GO, VIDUS, UHS, Op Dep Bulgaria, Kreek, deCODE, COGA, CaTS2-MOLE, CATS-PERTHUNT, ALIVE, ADAA; the Ontario GENOA study (row 117) is NOT among them. Unlocated: members span the United States, Canada, Iceland, Bulgaria and Australia but no source sentence lists the countries. 4 GWAS Catalog studies (PMID:36207451) tagged GENOA are this consortium. Acronym GENOA clashes with review row GENOA (Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy, not yet in COHO) and with row 117 (Ontario Genetics of Opioid Addiction study); curator to add editor notes. No COHO term matches GENOA or opioid (coho.sh).

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Study
other synonyms: GENetics of Opioid Addiction|Genetics of Opioid Addiction research collaborative
example title: A genome-wide association, polygenic risk score and sex study on opioid use disorder treatment outcomes.
example quote: Data were collected as part of the GENetics of Opioid Addiction (GENOA) and Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response (POST) programs.
definition: A prospective cohort of adults with opioid use disorder receiving treatment at Canadian Addiction Treatment Centre clinics across Ontario, Canada, recruited in 2013–2016 in collaboration with McMaster University to identify factors, including genetic risk factors, associated with opioid use and treatment outcomes.
location quote: Briefly, participants (nGENOA = 1536, nPOST = 3319) were recruited from 76 CATC sites across Ontario, Canada (GENOA, 2013–2016, POST, 2018–present).
note: McMaster/CATC study in Ontario, distinct from the NIDA Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium (row 116): it is not in the consortium member list (PMC9546890 Supplementary Table 1), so no parent. POST (PGS cohort POST, Pharmacogenetics of Opioid Substitution Treatment Response) is a separate sister cohort from the same group and clinics, recruited 2018-present with similar methods ("The GENOA and POST studies are prospective cohort studies conducted in collaboration with the Canadian Addiction Treatment Centre (CATC) and McMaster University."); neither is part of the other. The 4 GWAS Catalog studies of PMID:38102185 are tagged both GENOA and POST and pool 924 GENOA and 1327 POST participants. PMID:28347350 calls it the "Genetics of Opioid Addiction research collaborative" (data 2011–2016, so recruitment dates vary by source). Label may need disambiguation from row 116 (e.g. adding "(Ontario)"). Acronym GENOA clashes with review row GENOA (Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy, not yet in COHO) and with row 116; curator to add editor notes. No COHO match (coho.sh).

label: deCODE Health Study
other synonyms: deCODE health study
example title: The genetic architecture of age-related hearing impairment revealed by genome-wide association analysis.
example quote: We conducted a GWAS of ARHI in three datasets obtained from the deCODE health study (DHS)24, the National Institute of Hearing and Speech in Iceland (NIHSI) and the UKB (Fig. 1, Supplementary Table 2).
definition: A general-population sample of Icelanders, enriched for carriers of rare and potentially high-impact mutations, comprehensively phenotyped by deCODE genetics in Iceland (e.g. audiometry, speech recordings, DXA body composition, plasma proteomics) and combined with the Icelandic genotype and sequence data for genetic association studies.
location quote: Speech samples were obtained from 14,144 Icelandic participants as a part of the deCODE Health Study in Iceland, which involves comprehensive phenotyping of a general population sample.
parent quote: These phenotypes were collected through the deCODE Health Study and other research projects at deCODE genetics.
note: GWAS tag DHS: 4 studies over 2 PMIDs, overloaded - deCODE Health Study only in GCST012442 (PMID:34108613; the paper expands DHS as "deCODE health study"); GCST90502911/3/4 (PMID:40216759) use DHS for the Diabetes Heart Study (review row DiabHS). Acronym DHS kept per the follow-up rule; it clashes with COHO:0000054 Dortmund Health Study (synonym DHS; the PGS Catalog id DHS also means Dortmund) and with review row DiabHS (Diabetes Heart Study, acronym DHS, not yet in COHO) - curator to add editor notes to all three. Parent: review row deCODE (deCODE genetics Icelandic cohort), whose definition already names the deCODE Health Study; the parent quote says DHS is one of the research projects at deCODE genetics through which that Icelandic sample was phenotyped. Definition also draws on PMC10256171 (DXA and speech) and PMC12982484 ("The deCODE Health study conducted proteomic profiling on blood plasma samples from 35,559 Icelanders using the SomaScan platform..."). No dedicated profile paper found (PMID:34108613 cites refs 24/25 for it); recruitment dates not found.

label: Qatar Biobank
example title: A Whole-Genome Sequencing Association Study of Low Bone Mineral Density Identifies New Susceptibility Loci in the Phase I Qatar Biobank Cohort.
example quote: Here we sequenced the whole genomes of 3000 individuals from the Qatar Biobank and conducted genome-wide association analyses to identify genetic risk factors associated with low BMD in the Qatari population.
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of adult Qatari nationals and long-term residents (living in Qatar for at least 15 years), recruited by the Qatar Biobank from December 2012 with extensive lifestyle, clinical, imaging and biological-sample data and long-term follow-up, to study the causes, progression and burden of disease in the Qatari population.
location quote: Qatar Biobank will provide a powerful resource to investigate the major determinants of ill-health and well-being in Qatar, providing valuable insights into the current and future public health burden that faces the country.
note: 42 GWAS Catalog studies tagged QBB over 13 PMIDs (example GCST90093097-101 tagged QBB only). Qatar IS in gaz_xrefs.tsv (dbpedia:Qatar, GAZ:00005286) - contrary to the batch brief and to the QGP row note, which both say it is not. PGS other name "Qatar Genome Program (QGP)" is a distinct entity: review row QGP (Qatar Genome Program) sequences QBB volunteers and should be isSubCohortOf this term (QGP row already carries the quote "...6045 healthy volunteers from the Qatar Biobank (QBB) released as part of Qatar Genome Program (QGP)"), so it is not added as a synonym here. Tag overlap: no study carries both QBB and QGP tags, but the 1305 QGP-tagged studies analyse Qatar Biobank participants too. No COHO match or clash for QBB/Qatar. No parent (Qatar Foundation is the host organisation, not a cohort).

other synonyms: Partners HealthCare Biobank
example title: Discovery of genomic loci associated with sleep apnea risk through multi-trait GWAS analysis with snoring.
example quote: The authors want to acknowledge Partners HealthCare Biobank for providing samples, genomic data, and health information.
note: Same biobank as review row MGBB under its former name; see row MGBB for definition, location and evidence; merge PHB and "Partners HealthCare Biobank" into it (MGBB row already has "Partners Biobank"). Name link, verified verbatim in PMC12749686 (the MGBB example paper, PMID:41298473): "MGBB, previously known as Partners Biobank, is an integrated research initiative based in Boston, Massachusetts." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12749686/fullTextXML). GWAS tag PHB exists: 60 studies over 5 PMIDs (28861588 x50, 36525587 x4, 36171425 x3, 37245863 x2, 40050429 x1) - the MGBB row note did not know of it. No COHO clash for PHB or Partners.

label: Reykjavik Study
other synonyms: Reykjavík Study
example title: C-reactive protein in migraine sufferers similar to that of non-migraineurs: the Reykjavik Study.
example quote: The Reykjavik Study is a large, population-based cohort study, which started in 1967.
definition: A population-based cohort of men born 1907–1934 and women born 1908–1935, randomly selected from residents of the Reykjavik area, examined at the Heart Preventive Clinic in Reykjavik from 1967 and followed since in Iceland by the Icelandic Heart Association, to study cardiovascular disease and its risk factors.
location quote: This cohort of men and women born between 1907 and 1935 has been followed in Iceland since 1967 by the Icelandic Heart Association.
note: Added 2026-09-23 as the parent of AGES (Age, Gene/Environment Susceptibility-Reykjavik Study), which PMID:17351290 says is drawn from it. No COHO term matched Reykjavik (coho-edit.owl grep 2026-09-23). No GWAS Catalog or PGS Catalog tag, so the example is a paper (open-access text via BioC); no acronym found in the sources, so none given. Label without the leading "The"; accented spelling Reykjavík Study appears in several paper titles (e.g. PMID:12653870, PMID:23232723). The separately sampled Reykjavik Study for the Young (begun 1972, same paper) is not included in this term. Purpose (cardiovascular disease and risk factors) is inferred from the Heart Preventive Clinic setting and the cardiovascular risk factor assessments described in PMID:17351290; no single design paper was fetched.

label: Human Functional Genomics Project
example title: The Human Functional Genomics Project: Understanding Generation of Diversity.
example quote: Studies from the Human Functional Genomics Project, presented in Cell and other Cell Press journals, integrate environmental and genetic factors with the direction and magnitude of immune responses to decipher inflammatory disease pathogenesis.
definition: A research programme based at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, that collects distinct cohorts of healthy volunteers and patients (among them 500FG, 200FG, 300BCG, 300OB, 300DM and 2000HIV) profiled with genetic, immunological and other omics data, to identify the genetic and non-genetic determinants of human immune and cytokine responses.
location quote: The cohort comprises 197 healthy adults working as foresters from the ‘Geldersch Landschap’, ‘Hoge Veluwe’, ‘Twickel’, and ‘Kroondomein het Loo’ in the Netherlands.
parent quote: Both cohorts are part of the Human Functional Genomics Project (wwww.humanfunctionalgenomics.org), aimed at identifying the genetic and non-genetic determinants of the immune response.
note: Added 2026-09-23 as the parent of 500FG. Typed as an aggregation: its projects page lists distinct cohorts (500FG, 200FG, 2000HIV, BCG-PRIME, 300BCG, INFLUENZA-SHINGRIX, 300OB, 300DM) and says "The Human Functional Genomics Projects have over 20 sub-projects"; children link with memberOf (hasCohort from this term). The parent quote and parent URL in this row are NOT for a parent of HFGP: they are the evidence for linking the existing COHO:0000208 (300BCG) to this term as a member (COHO:0000208 memberOf HFGP), to be added when this term is minted; the parent quote is two sentences of the Methods of PMC10851559 joined by " | " ("Both cohorts" are 500FG and 300BCG; "wwww." is verbatim). No COHO match for Human Functional Genomics/HFGP (coho-edit.owl grep 2026-09-23; COHO:0000208's definition already mentions the project in text). No GWAS/PGS Catalog tag, so the example is the 2016 Cell editorial (abstract). Radboud University Medical Center is from the 500FG paper ("in the Radboud University Medical Center, the Netherlands", PMC5787854) and the site address (Geert Grooteplein Zuid 10, Nijmegen); the About page also lists team members in Germany, Romania, USA, Tanzania, Indonesia and India, but only the Netherlands is asserted as a collection country. The task brief cited the 500FG quote as PMC5787845; that PMCID is an unrelated rice/wheat paper, the correct one is PMC5787854 (PMID:27814508). Child-link quote trimmed 2026-09-23 to one verbatim sentence; "both cohorts" are 500FG and 300BCG, named in the two preceding sentences of the same paragraph (PMC10851559).

input name: NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study
label: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III
other synonyms: NHLBI Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study|National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study|Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study III
example title: Genome-wide association study of early ischaemic stroke risk in Brazilian individuals with sickle cell disease implicates ADAMTS2 and CDK18 and uncovers novel loci.
example quote: This was conducted within the Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort Study as part of the Recipient Epidemiology Donor Evaluation Study III (REDS-III).
definition: A seven-year multicentre transfusion-medicine research programme launched in 2011 by the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, with a domestic component of four blood centres and 12 hospitals and international programmes in Brazil, China and South Africa, which built linked donor, donation and transfusion-recipient databases and ran more than 25 focused studies of blood donors and recipients, such as RBC-Omics and the Brazil sickle cell disease cohort.
location quote: The international component consists of distinct programs in Brazil, China, and South Africa, which involve US and in-country investigators.
note: Added 2026-09-23 as the parent of RBC-Omics. Typed as an aggregation: PMID:24188564 calls REDS-III a "multicenter transfusion safety research initiative" of domestic and international programs with "more than 25 focused research protocols", which include RBC-Omics parts I and II and the Brazil SCD cohort (BioC PMC4383641); children link with memberOf. 1 GWAS Catalog study (GCST90270269, PMID:36602125, the REDS-III Brazil SCD cohort). Location quote is two sentences of the same abstract joined by " | ". No COHO match or acronym clash (coho-edit.owl grep for REDS/Recipient Epidemiology 2026-09-23). Not in this review and not merged here: the separate PGS/GWAS tag REDS ("Recipient Epidemiology and Donor evaluation Study", 11 studies all from PMID:38964323, which used 13,029 REDS donors, i.e. the RBC-Omics sample) - a curator should decide whether that tag belongs on RBC-Omics or here; and the successor programme REDS-IV-P (PMID:35441384), a distinct programme. Europe PMC full text of PMC10155195 and PMC4383641 returned errors, so the NCBI BioC version was used. Location quote trimmed 2026-09-23 to one verbatim sentence of the abstract (PMID:24188564).

input name: Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health
label: Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health
other synonyms: Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health|Kaiser Permanente Northern California Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health|Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health
example title: Genome-wide analysis identifies genetic effects on reproductive success and ongoing natural selection at the FADS locus.
example quote: Data used in this study were provided by the Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health (RPGEH): Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging (GERA)
definition: A research resource developed by the Kaiser Permanente Northern California Division of Research from consenting members of the KPNC health plan, linking surveys, biospecimens and electronic health records and including the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohort and a pregnancy cohort, for research on the genetic and environmental determinants of common, age-related complex health conditions.
location quote: The GERA cohort is part of the Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health (RPGEH).
note: Added 2026-09-23 as the parent of GERA and IMPACT_KPNC. Label: the literature still calls it the (Kaiser Permanente) Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health; Europe PMC hits 2023-2026: 73 for the full name vs 47 for "Kaiser Permanente Research Bank". The Research Bank is not a new name for RPGEH but a larger, Kaiser Permanente-wide collection that contains it: "Data used in this study (beyond summary statistics described above) were provided by the Kaiser Permanente Research Bank from the Kaiser Permanente Research Bank collection, which includes the Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health." (PMC13340790; likewise PMC9023580, "the KPRB collection, which includes the Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health (RPGEH) and the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging (GERA)"). So Kaiser Permanente Research Bank / KPRB is deliberately NOT added as a synonym, contrary to the brief; a curator may want a separate KPRB term later (PGS id KP "Kaiser Permanente", 36 GWAS studies, is also unassigned). Typed as a cohort (a health-plan biobank, like UK Biobank) with GERA and the RPGEH pregnancy cohort as sub-cohorts. PGS Catalog has two ids for it, RPGEH and RPEGH (a transposition, name "Kaiser Permanente Research Program on Genes, Environment, and Health", no GWAS studies); both kept as acronyms. The 3 GWAS Catalog studies tagged RPGEH (PMID:36864135) actually used RPGEH/GERA data (supplementary note quoted); a curator may prefer to move the tag to GERA. Example quote is from the Supplementary Information PDF of PMID:36864135 (text extracted with pdftotext, line breaks joined); the main text does not name RPGEH. Location quote names Northern California (country implied). No COHO match or acronym clash (coho-edit.owl grep for RPGEH/RPEGH/Kaiser/Research Bank 2026-09-23).

label: Africa America Diabetes Mellitus Study
other synonyms: Africa America Diabetes Mellitus|AADM study
example title: Genome-wide analyses of multiple obesity-related cytokines and hormones informs biology of cardiometabolic traits.
example quote: We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in 4432 continental Africans, enrolled from Ghana, Kenya, and Nigeria as part of the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus (AADM) study
definition: A genetic epidemiology study of type 2 diabetes begun in 1997 as a collaboration of West African and US investigators, enrolling affected sib-pairs with type 2 diabetes and unaffected controls in Ghana and Nigeria and later participants in Eldoret, Kenya, to map type 2 diabetes susceptibility genes in the West African ancestral populations of African Americans.
location quote: Data were collected in three cities in Nigeria (Ibadan, Enugu, and Lagos), two cities in Ghana (Accra, and Kumasi), and in the city of Eldoret in Kenya.
note: 99 GWAS Catalog studies over 5 PMIDs (90 from PMID:34620218, which also carries the HUFS tag because HUFS was its African American replication cohort; 26507551 is the AADM metabolic syndrome GWAS of Ghanaians and Nigerians; 35546142, 34117260 and 38190104 are meta-analyses including AADM). No match in COHO (coho_list.txt, coho-edit.owl and components grep for AADM, 'Africa America', 'Diabetes Mellitus' 2026-09-23) or the review file; no acronym clash. Label adds 'Study' as the design paper does ('the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus (AADM) study', PMID:11164120; titles of PMID:14988271 and PMID:15652721 use 'the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus (AADM) Study'); PGS name kept as other synonym. Definition: design, 1997 start, sib-pair/control enrolment and aim from the PMID:11164120 abstract (Ann Epidemiol 2001, not open access); Kenya (Eldoret) and the 'cross-sectional study comprising data on individuals residing in sub-Saharan Africa' description from PMC8499470 Methods. Example quote from the PMID:34620218 abstract, location quote from its full-text Methods. The study is run from NHGRI's Center for Research on Genomics and Global Health (Rotimi, Adeyemo) - not quoted, not in definition.

label: Danish Blood Donor Study
other synonyms: DBDS Genomic Cohort
example title: A genome-wide association study of social trust in 33,882 Danish blood donors.
example quote: In this study, we investigate the genetic underpinnings of social trust in n = 33,882 participants of the Danish Blood Donor Study (DBDS) using a validated questionnaire.
definition: An ongoing nationwide prospective cohort of blood donors aged 18-70 at inclusion, recruited at Danish blood donation facilities since 2010 (all facilities in Denmark by 2015), with questionnaires, plasma samples, genotyping and linkage to national health registries for research on donor health and general public health.
location quote: The cohort was initiated in 2010 and by 2015 it covered all blood donation facilities in Denmark.
note: 96 GWAS Catalog studies over 17 PMIDs (24 from PMID:42521817, fibromyalgia; 22 from PMID:40205036, osteoarthritis), mostly deCODE-led meta-analyses listing the 'DBDS Genomic Consortium'; PMID:38228779 (social trust) is a DBDS-only GWAS. No COHO term or review-file/tier-B row matches DBDS, 'blood donor' or 'Danish Blood' (coho-edit.owl, coho_list, review_names grepped 2026-09-23). Definition from the Cohort Profile (PMID:36194120, OA full text PMC10244044): 'The DBDS is an ongoing, national prospective cohort of blood donors.'; 138,491 participants as of February 2022, age span at inclusion 18-70. 'DBDS Genomic Cohort' is the name of the genotyped subset (title of PMID:31182452, checked in Europe PMC search) - curator may prefer it as a separate sub-cohort or drop it. Example quote from the OA full text of PMID:38228779 (its introduction/discussion), location quote from the Cohort Profile full text.

example title: Genome-wide analyses of multiple obesity-related cytokines and hormones informs biology of cardiometabolic traits.
example quote: Replication analyses were performed using data on 7990 AA from five different cohorts: the Howard University Family Study (HUFS) [32]
definition: A population-based family study of African Americans from the Washington, DC metropolitan area, enrolling randomly ascertained families and unrelated individuals through Howard University without selection on any phenotype, to study the genetic and environmental basis of common complex diseases including hypertension, obesity and type 2 diabetes.
location quote: The HUFS (Principal Investigator: CNR) was a study of AA from the Washington DC metropolitan area (USA) and was designed to investigate the genetic and environmental basis of common complex traits such as hypertension, obesity, and T2D [32].

No match in COHO (grep for HUFS, Howard 2026-09-23) or the review file; no acronym clash. Definition from PMC2702100 (PMID:19609347, the first HUFS GWAS): 'a population based family study of African Americans in the Washington metropolitan area', objectives to 'enroll and examine a randomly ascertained cohort of African-American families, along with a set of unrelated individuals', 'families were not ascertained based on any phenotype'; T2D from PMC8499470. Example and location quotes from the PMC8499470 full-text Methods.

example title: Genome-wide analyses identify SCN5A as a susceptibility locus for premature atrial contraction frequency.
example quote: Genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors (GAPP) is a population-based prospective cohort study involving a representative sample of healthy adults aged 25–41 years residing in the Principality of Liechtenstein (Conen et al., 2013).
definition: A population-based prospective cohort of a representative sample of healthy adults aged 25-41 in the Principality of Liechtenstein, enrolled from June 2010 without cardiovascular disease, diabetes or severe obesity, with ambulatory blood pressure, Holter ECG, spirometry, sleep oximetry and blood, urine and genetic sampling, and followed up every 3-5 years to study genetic and phenotypic predictors of cardiovascular risk factors in young adults.
location quote: Genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors (GAPP) is a population-based prospective cohort study involving a representative sample of healthy adults aged 25–41 years residing in the Principality of Liechtenstein (Conen et al., 2013).
note: 54 GWAS Catalog studies over 5 PMIDs (40181193x32, 36050321x18, 35228297x2, 36267918x1, 40050429x1). No match for gapp or liechtenstein in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. Label from the design paper title (Conen et al. 2013, Swiss Med Wkly, PMID:23299990), whose abstract also says 'The genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors (GAPP) study'; the PGS name (with 'The' and '(Liechtenstein)' appended) is kept as synonym. Example quote and location quote from the cohort description in PMC9576575 (PMID:36267918, the same GCST as the SAPALDIA example; non-breaking space in 'et al.' as in the source); definition from the PMID:23299990 abstract. Country not in gaz_xrefs.tsv: Liechtenstein (proposed DBpedia name Liechtenstein). COVI-GAPP (a COVID-19 wearable-sensor study in Liechtenstein, PMID:38446766) is a separate study, not tagged here.

example quote: The Women’s Genome Health Study (WGHS) is a population-based, prospective cohort of initially healthy, female North American health care professionals at least 45 years old at baseline, representing participants in the Women’s Health Study (WHS) who provided a blood sample at baseline and consented for blood-based analyses.
definition: A prospective genome-wide association cohort of more than 25,000 initially healthy American female health professionals aged 45 or older from the Women's Health Study who gave a baseline blood sample, followed since 1992 for incident cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes and other outcomes.
location quote: The primary aim of the Women's Genome Health Study (WGHS) is to create a comprehensive, fully searchable genome-wide database of >360 000 single nucleotide polymorphisms among at least 25 000 initially healthy American women participating in the ongoing NIH-funded Women's Health Study (WHS).
parent quote: The primary aim of the Women's Genome Health Study (WGHS) is to create a comprehensive, fully searchable genome-wide database of >360 000 single nucleotide polymorphisms among at least 25 000 initially healthy American women participating in the ongoing NIH-funded Women's Health Study (WHS).

example title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide meta-analysis of 56,241 individuals identifies known and novel cross-population and ancestry-specific associations as novel risk loci for Alzheimer's disease.

definition: A US consortium that assembles genome-wide genotype data and harmonized phenotypes from many case-control, family-based, population-based and longitudinal Alzheimer disease cohorts, in more than 30 GWAS datasets of several ancestries, for genetic studies of late-onset Alzheimer disease.
location quote: This was a meta-analysis of genetic association studies in case-control, family-based, population-based, and longitudinal AD-related cohorts from the US Alzheimer’s Disease Genetics Consortium, the Alzheimer’s Disease Sequencing Project, the UK Biobank, the Finnish health registry, and the US Million Veterans Program.
note: Tag ADGC: 49 GCSTs, 16 PMIDs; abstracts of 40676597, 41268768 and 39250132 and OA texts of 40708016 (PMC12288278) and 34122051 (PMC8194397) name the Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium; the others were not checked. Its member datasets include the NIA Alzheimer's Disease Center (ADC) samples (row NACC / second ADC row) and cohorts such as ACT (row ACT) and ROSMAP, but no member quotes were gathered for hasCohort links. Label is the literature form; PGS name ('Alzheimer Disease Genetic Consortium') and the variant 'Alzheimer's Disease Genetic Consortium' (PMID:41268768 abstract) kept as other synonyms. input name: Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America
label: Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America
other synonyms: CANDELA cohort
example title: Automatic landmarking identifies new loci associated with face morphology and implicates Neanderthal introgression in human nasal shape.
example quote: The 6486 individuals examined here are part of the CANDELA cohort, collected in five Latin American countries21.
definition: A sample of about 7,300 adult volunteers of mixed African, European and Native American ancestry, mostly university students and staff (and, in Chile, mainly soldiers), recruited by a consortium of Latin American and UK groups in México City, Medellín, Lima, Arica and Porto Alegre and characterised for genome-wide genotypes, physical appearance, facial photographs and self-perceived ancestry, to study admixture and the genetics of physical traits in Latin America.
location quote: Recruitment took place mainly in five locations: México City (México), Medellín (Colombia), Lima (Perú), Arica (Chile) and Porto Alegre (Brazil).
note: Countries not in gaz_xrefs.tsv: Colombia (dbpedia:Colombia) and Chile (dbpedia:Chile); Mexico, Peru and Brazil are there. Typed as a cohort, not an aggregation, although it is named a consortium: the consortium recruited one sample under a common protocol (PMC4177621 abstract: 'We estimated individual ancestry proportions in a sample of 7,342 subjects ascertained in five countries') and the GWAS papers call it 'the CANDELA cohort' (PMC10167347); it does not collect pre-existing cohorts. In the HISLA consortium paper (PMID:35399580, 10 of the 49 tagged studies) CANDELA is a member ('HISLA stage 1 includes 17 studies and one consortium (Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America [CANDELA]17)', PMC8990175); HISLA is not in COHO, not in the review file and not a tier-B row, so no parent is given (a curator could add a HISLA aggregation). 49 GWAS Catalog studies over 2 PMIDs (PMID:37156940 x39 face morphology; PMID:35399580 x10 anthropometry). The same PMID:35399580 also carries GWAS tags 'Mexico City 1' and 'Mexico City 2' (10 studies each) for other HISLA studies, which are not CANDELA's México City recruits (not checked further; not tier-B rows). Location and recruitment from Ruiz-Linares et al. 2014 (PMC4177621), which is reference 21 for the CANDELA cohort in PMC10167347 but does not itself use the word CANDELA. Example quote ends with the citation digits '21' as in the XML. No COHO or review-file match for CANDELA, 'Latin America' or HISLA (coho_list.txt, review_names.tsv, coho-edit.owl grep 2026-09-23); no clash.

example quote: Here, we compared CH in 136,401 participants from the Mexico City Prospective Study (MCPS) to 416,118 individuals from the UK Biobank (UKB)
definition: A prospective cohort of more than 150,000 adults aged 35 and over, recruited in 1998-2004 from the contiguous urban districts of Coyoacán and Iztapalapa in Mexico City with the University of Oxford, and followed to investigate known and new risk factors for mortality in people of Mexican descent; its participants have exome and genome-wide genetic data.
location quote: MCPS is a prospective cohort of more than 150,000 adults, aged at least 35 years, who were recruited between 1998 and 2004 from the contiguous urban districts of Coyoacán and Iztapalapa in Mexico City23,55.
note: 49 GWAS Catalog studies over 6 PMIDs (PMID:39948438 x25, PMID:37308787 x18, PMID:35999217 x2, PMID:41735279 x2, PMID:35551307 x1, PMID:38190104 x1); PGS REST lists MCPS for 2 developed and 8 evaluated scores. Not the same as COHO:0000114 Mexican Biobank (a national INSP biobank across all 32 states) or COHO:0000050 Diabetes in Mexico Study (type 2 diabetes cases and controls in Mexico City): MCPS is a separate population-based prospective cohort of two Mexico City districts, run with the University of Oxford CTSU ('Individual-level MCPS data may be requested from the Data and Sample Access Policy available on the study's Oxford-hosted webpage (http://www.ctsu.ox.ac.uk/research/mcps)', PMC11906367; 'The MCPS study was approved by the Mexican Ministry of Health, the Mexican National Council for Science and Technology and the University of Oxford'). Aim from PMC10335934 ('The MCPS is a large prospective cohort of 150,000 individuals recruited between 1998 and 2004 with a major aim to investigate the known and new risk factors for mortality in individuals of Mexican descent'). Other synonym 'Mexico City Prospective Cohort' is used once in PMC11906367's summary line. Location quote contains a thin space (U+2009) between '35' and 'years' and ends with citation digits '23,55', as in the XML. No COHO or review-file match for MCPS or 'Mexico City' (coho_list.txt, review_names.tsv, coho-edit.owl grep 2026-09-23); no clash.

label: Airwave Health Monitoring Study
example title: Discovery of rare variants associated with blood pressure regulation through meta-analysis of 1.3 million individuals.
example quote: We thank all participants in the Airwave Health Monitoring Study.
definition: An occupational cohort of police officers and staff of police forces across Great Britain, enrolled from 2004 (42,112 participants by the end of 2012, most of whom attended a health screening with questionnaires, food diaries, physical and cognitive measurements and stored blood and urine), set up to evaluate possible health risks of the TETRA digital radio system and broadened to study the health of the police workforce.
location quote: a digital communication system used by police forces and other emergency services in Great Britain since 2001
note: 60 GWAS Catalog studies over 4 PMIDs (tag Airwave 48 studies/3 PMIDs: 32888493x30, 33230300x16, 37679419x2; tag AIRWAVE 12 studies/1 PMID: 34187551). AIRWAVE and Airwave differ only by case, so one acronym is kept (Airwave, also the PGS id). No match for airwave in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. None of the four tagged papers names Airwave in its Europe PMC main text (32888493 is not open access; BioC text also lacks it); the example quote is a single line of the study-specific acknowledgements in EMS118016-supplement-Supplementary_Information.pdf inside the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles zip of PMC7610439 (the same file lists the cohort as AIRWAVE with n=13102, and its Supplementary Tables give the full name Airwave Health Monitoring Study). label: Cohorte Lausannoise
other synonyms: CoLaus Study|Cohort Lausanne
example title: Genetic determinants of zinc homeostasis and its role in cardiometabolic diseases.
example quote: We conducted a GWAS of urinary zinc levels in three prospective cohorts - SKIPOGH (Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension, N = 896) [29,30], CoLaus|PsyCoLaus (Cohort Lausanne, N = 4,542) [31] and GCKD (German Chronic Kidney Disease study, N = 4,822) [32]
definition: A population-based cohort of a random sample of 6,188 Caucasian adults aged 35 to 75 living in Lausanne, Switzerland, extensively phenotyped and genotyped genome-wide at baseline to study the prevalence and genetic determinants of cardiovascular risk factors and the metabolic syndrome, and followed up prospectively (with its psychiatric arm PsyCoLaus) from 2003 for cardiovascular events and mortality.
location quote: In order to assess the prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors (CVRFs) in the Caucasian population of Lausanne, Switzerland, we conducted a population-based study (Colaus Study).
note: 81 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs (tag CoLaus 48 studies/6 PMIDs, 36 from PMID:40537477; tag COLAUS 33 studies/2 PMIDs, 32 from PMID:40181193). COLAUS and CoLaus differ only by case, so one acronym is kept. No match for colaus or lausann in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. Label is the PGS name, which the cohort uses in French (title of PMID:31910756: 'Différences socio-économiques dans la Cohorte Lausannoise CoLaus'); the English literature mostly says 'CoLaus|PsyCoLaus' (the combined name cannot be kept as synonym because | is the list separator here) or 'CoLaus Study' (PMID:18366642). Example quote from the main text of PMID:41325371 (zinc GWAS), where CoLaus|PsyCoLaus contributes 4,542 participants; it contains thin spaces around = as in the source. Definition from the design paper abstract (Firmann et al. 2008, PMID:18366642) and the follow-up period (2003-2021) from the PMID:38388190 abstract ('Population-based prospective study conducted in Lausanne, Switzerland, with a follow-up between 2003 and 2021'). PsyCoLaus is the psychiatric sub-study of the same participants; a curator may prefer a separate term for it.

example quote: the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study (MCCS)41

Definition from PMC12490524 Methods ("a prospective study that recruited 41,513 middle-aged and older Australians (99 % aged between 40 and 69 years, 59 % females) of white European origin between 1990 and 1994 (baseline) (Milne et al., 2017). label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey
other synonyms: Tracking Adolescents Individual Lives Survey|TRAILS population cohort
example title: Genetic determinants of childhood blood pressure and heart rate in relation to adult health outcomes: the consortium of childhood blood pressure.
example quote: A.J.O. has received research funding from the Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research and the Biobanking and Biomolecular Resources Research Infrastructure to support the TRAILS cohort
definition: A prospective population cohort of 2,230 children born between October 1989 and September 1991 who lived in the North of the Netherlands, assessed from about age 11 in 2001/02 and followed into young adulthood with repeated assessments of mental health, social development and physical health, psychiatric diagnostic interviews, registry linkage and genome-wide genotyping.
location quote: The population cohort includes participants born between 1 October 1989 and 30 September 1991, who lived in the North of The Netherlands at the time of the baseline assessment in 2001/02.
note: 45 GWAS Catalog studies over 5 PMIDs (PMID:40537477 x36 lipids x psychosocial interactions, PMID:42036355 x5 childhood blood pressure, PMID:40962958 x2 childhood ADHD, PMID:34059833, PMID:35378236). No COHO or review-file match for TRAILS/Tracking Adolescents (grep 2026-09-23). The TRAILS study 'consists of a population cohort (N=2230) and a clinical cohort (N=543)' (PMID:25431468 abstract); the GWAS Catalog tags the clinical cohort separately as TRAILSCC (tier C row 'Tracking Adolescents Individual Lives Survey (TRAILS) Clinical Cohort', 5 studies, e.g. alongside TRAILS on GCST90797639), so this term is the population cohort and is minted as a cohort. A curator could instead make TRAILS an aggregation of the population and clinical cohorts (as COHO:0000202 SHIP is for SHIP-START and SHIP-TREND). The tagged papers name the cohort only in supplementary tables; the example quote is from the author declarations of PMC13533560. Label follows the cohort profile title (capital TR); PGS name without apostrophe kept as synonym. Definition and location from PMC4339762 (PMID:25431468). The offspring cohort TRAILS NEXT (PMID:35462400) is separate.

label: ADDITION-PRO Study
