example title: Genome-wide association study identifies host genetic variants influencing oral microbiota diversity and metabolic health.

definition: A population-based longitudinal cohort of 2,082 Danish adults at different levels of diabetes risk, sampled from the 16,136 high-risk individuals identified by the 2001–2006 stepwise diabetes screening programme in Danish general practice of the Danish arm of ADDITION-Europe, examined in 2009–2011 with detailed cardiometabolic phenotyping and followed for cardiovascular disease and death.
location quote: 16,136 eligible individuals were identified at high risk following participation in a stepwise screening programme in Danish general practice between 2001 and 2006.
parent quote: The ADDITION-PRO study is nested within the Danish arm (ADDITION-DK) of the ADDITION-Europe study [3,8].
note: 44 GWAS Catalog studies, 1 PMID (PMID:38926497, oral microbiota GWAS in 610 participants). Grepped coho-edit.owl, coho_list and review_names for ADDITION: no term. No expansion of the name was found (protocol paper PMID:23241242); label 'ADDITION-PRO Study' as in the titles of PMID:28509724 and PMID:40635178 (Europe PMC search), so that the acronym ADDITION-PRO differs from the label. The protocol full text says ADDITION-PRO invited 'individuals at different levels of diabetes risk identified from the stepwise screening programme of the Danish arm of the ADDITION-Europe study', i.e. mostly screened people without diabetes who were not in the ADDITION-Denmark treatment trial itself; PMID:38926497 calls it 'a subsidiary study of the Danish arm of the ADDITION trial'. isSubCohortOf follows the protocol's 'nested within' wording - curator to confirm. Example quote from the PMID:38926497 abstract, location quote from the PMID:23241242 abstract, parent quote from the PMID:23241242 full text (Methods).

input name: Arthroplasty and the Genetics of Osteoarthritis
label: Arthroplasty and the Genetics of Osteoarthritis
other synonyms: ARGO study
example title: Deciphering osteoarthritis genetics across 826,690 individuals from 9 populations.
example quote: The ARGO study, was set up to investigate the genetic architecture of hip and knee OA in a Greek population.
definition: A Greek collection of more than 1,500 well-phenotyped patients with severe hip or knee osteoarthritis undergoing total joint replacement, recruited in hospitals of Athens (2015-2017) and Larissa together with healthy controls, set up to study the genetic architecture of osteoarthritis.
location quote: More than 1,500 patients with severe OA, undergoing hip and/or knee total joint replacement were recruited from the cities of Athens and Larissa.
note: 43 GWAS Catalog studies over 2 PMIDs (40205036x22, 34450027x21). No match for argo, arthroplasty or larissa in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt, the review file or the curation tables. The label is the PGS name; its expansion of ARGO could not be verified in any fetched text (Europe PMC finds no 'arthroplasty and genetics' phrase; the papers, EGA study EGAS00001000917 'ARGO_GWAS' and PMC6251918 use only 'ARGO'/'the ARGO study'), so a curator should confirm it or relabel the term 'ARGO study'. PMID:34450027 (PMC8459317) analyses two sub-collections, ARGO-Larissa (knee OA cases undergoing total knee arthroplasty, city of Larissa; raw data in EGA EGAS00001000917) and ARGO-Athens (four Athens hospitals, February 2015-March 2017), described under one ARGO study; they are not tagged separately, so one cohort is proposed. Example and location quotes from the PMC8459317 cohort descriptions; definition also from the EGA study description ('The ARGO study is an ongoing collection of well-phenotyped OA patients undergoing total joint replacement and is based in Greece.') and PMC6251918 (PMID:30470734: 'ARGO comprises osteoarthritis cases and healthy controls from Larisa, Greece.').

example title: The Pharmacogenetics of Statin Therapy on Clinical Events: No Evidence that Genetic Variation Affects Statin Response on Myocardial Infarction.
example quote: The Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk (PROSPER) trial was supported by an investigator-initiated grant from Bristol-Myers Squibb, USA.
definition: A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial population of 5,804 men and women aged 70 to 82 with pre-existing vascular disease or risk factors for it, screened in Scotland, Ireland and the Netherlands and randomised to pravastatin 40 mg/day or placebo for about 3.2 years to test whether statin treatment reduces coronary and cerebrovascular events in the elderly.
location quote: In Scotland, Ireland, and the Netherlands, 23,770 individuals were screened, and 5,804 subjects (2,804 men and 3,000 women), aged 70 to 82 years (average 75 years) and with baseline cholesterol 4.0-9.0 mmol/l, were randomised.
note: 38 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs (36050321x18, 36918541x8, 34732054x6, 40038546x2, 35069183x1, 35551307x1, 38652672x1, 40050429x1). No match for prosper or pravastatin in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. Typed as cohort: it is a trial population, like other trial cohorts in COHO. Example quote from the acknowledgements of PMID:35069183 (statin pharmacogenetics GWAS, PMC8769168), whose methods list PROSPER among two randomized controlled trials in stage one; its GWAS was done within the PHASE project (PHArmacogenetic Study of Statins in the Elderly at Risk), which a curator may want as a synonym or separate term. Definition and location quote from the abstracts of PMID:12097148 (baseline paper, open access) and PMID:12457784 (main results). Scotland mapped to United_Kingdom; the Irish centre was the University of Cork (author affiliations in PMC134480), hence Republic_of_Ireland.

note: 74 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs, under four case variants of one tag: GenSalt 37 (6 PMIDs), GENSALT 23 (PMID:40181193), GENSalt 8 (PMID:36477530), GenSALT 6 (PMID:38162683); one acronym (GenSalt, the study's own spelling) kept, as tier A did. No match in COHO (coho_list.txt, coho-edit.owl and components grep for GenSalt, Salt 2026-09-23) or the review file; no acronym clash. Label from the design paper abstract (PMID:17443206, J Hum Hypertens 2007; Europe PMC full text PMC2377400 returned HTTP 500), which is the source of the definition and location quote; PGS name (hyphenated, with 'Study') kept as other synonym. NHLBI funding (U01HL072507) per PMC10755672 acknowledgements.

label: Mass General Brigham Biobank
example title: Global multi-ancestry genome-wide analyses identify genes and biological pathways associated with thyroid cancer and benign thyroid diseases.
example quote: Y.W. contributed data and analyses from the Mass General Brigham Biobank.

label: Kaiser Permanente Research Bank
other synonyms: KP Research Bank|Kaiser Permanente
example title: Three genes associated with anterior and posterior cruciate ligament injury : a genome-wide association analysis.
example quote: Genome-wide association (GWA) analyses were performed using data from the Kaiser Permanente Research Board (KPRB) and the UK Biobank.
definition: A research resource of Kaiser Permanente, launched in May 2016 and built on the Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, that collects biospecimens and surveys linked to electronic health records from consenting adult members across Kaiser Permanente's eight US regions (about 396,000 consented by July 2021), with general, pregnancy and cancer cohorts.
location quote: The KP Research Bank (KPRB), a research resource within KP, is seeking to collect biospecimens and surveys from at least 400,000 adult members across the U.S. and linking that information to the EHR.
note: The GWAS tag KP (36 studies, 6 PMIDs) means more than one Kaiser Permanente resource, so it gets two rows (this one and the next, an existing-term row for GERA) with KP as a shared acronym. (1) KPRB: PMIDs 34169730 (ACL/PCL injury, OA PMC8244791), 34081057 (patellar tendinopathy) and 36068934 (chondromalacia), 1 study each, all say "Kaiser Permanente Research Board (KPRB)" (sic, for Research Bank) and use KP Northern California health records; PMC8244791: "Our analysis cohort included 83,414 individuals of European ancestry who were genotyped at 670,572 SNPs" (probably the GERA genotypes held by KPRB; not stated). (2) GERA: PMID:36929174 (3 studies) used Rashkin et al. 2020 summary statistics from the "Kaiser Permanente cohort", which the Rashkin abstract (PMID:32887889) names as "the Kaiser Permanente Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohorts"; PMID:39406924 (gout, 24 studies, the largest group; not OA) is probably GERA too: its medRxiv preprint (10.1101/2022.11.26.22281768, PDF fetched) says "Institutional Review Board of the Kaiser Foundation Research Institute provided ethical approval for the Kaiser Permanente sample set" and the only reference in it naming a Kaiser cohort is Kvale et al. 2015 "Genotyping informatics and quality control for 100,000 subjects in the Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging (GERA) cohort" - not stated outright, curator to check. (3) PMID:37196047 (diverticular disease, 6 studies, OA PMC10191288) is an eMERGE study whose per-site tags include KP for the eMERGE site "Kaiser Permanente Washington/University of Washington" (formerly Group Health Cooperative/UW), which is neither KPRB nor GERA; no named cohort for it (it may be the ACT study, tier-B row ACT, unverified), so no row; curator may re-tag those 6 GCSTs to eMERGE. The review row RPGEH (COHO:0000473) deliberately did not take KPRB as a synonym because KPRB contains RPGEH; this row mints KPRB as its own term, and RPGEH should get isSubCohortOf KPRB with the quote "Launched in May 2016, the KPRB is built on an existing repository (Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health, or RPGEH) of approximately 220,000 KP members with data and biospecimens collected primarily between 2007 and 2011 from members of KP Northern California, and to a smaller extent, Southern California [6]." (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC8876075/fullTextXML) - not entered as a parent here because the parent column is for this term's own parent. PGS name "Kaiser Permanente" is the organisation; kept as other synonym only because PGS uses it. Clash: KP also proposed for COHO:0000431 (next row). Location quote ends "across the U.S." inside a longer sentence; PMC8876075 also lists the regions "Colorado, Georgia, Hawai’i, Mid-Atlantic, Northern California, Northwest, Southern California, and Washington". COHO/review grep for KP/KPRB/Research Bank: KP only as substring (IMPACT_KPNC); no clash beyond the GERA row.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
example title: GWAS meta-analyses clarify the genetics of cervical phenotypes and inform risk stratification for cervical cancer.
example quote: 565 cases and 29 801 controls from Kaiser Permanente cohort
note: Second meaning of the GWAS tag KP (see row KP, which mints the Kaiser Permanente Research Bank and carries the PGS id): 27 of the 36 KP studies mean the GERA cohort. PMID:36929174 (3 studies; cervical phenotypes, OA PMC10244231) took its Kaiser data from Rashkin et al. 2020 ("565 cases and 29 801 controls from Kaiser Permanente cohort", quote, thin spaces as in the XML), and the Rashkin abstract (PMID:32887889, fetched) says the two cohorts were "the UK Biobank (408,786 European ancestry individuals; 48,961 cancer cases) and the Kaiser Permanente Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging cohorts". PMID:39406924 (gout, 24 studies) is probably GERA (see row KP note), unverified. Add KP as an acronym of existing COHO:0000431; it clashes with row KP (KPRB), so both terms need editor notes. PGS id left empty because the PGS cohort KP ("Kaiser Permanente") is assigned to row KP.

input name: Cancer Prevention Study II (including the Nutrition cohort)
label: Cancer Prevention Study
other synonyms: Cancer Prevention Study II|Cancer Prevention Study-II|Cancer Prevention Study II (including the Nutrition cohort)
example title: Genome-wide association study identifies tumor anatomical site-specific risk variants for colorectal cancer survival.
example quote: The following 15 ISACC studies were included: the Cancer Prevention Study-II (CPS-II)35
parent: Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium
parent quote: Cancer Prevention Study II (CPSII)
note: Existing COHO:0000024 Cancer Prevention Study (synonym CPS): its definition ("A cohort of adult men and women across all United States states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, enrolled by the American Cancer Society in 1982 ...", source cancer.org cps-2 page) and its example (PMID:37783704, quote "Cancer Prevention Study II (CPSII)") are already CPS-II, so this is the same cohort, not a sub-cohort; add CPSII and CPS-II as acronyms and the long forms as synonyms. The PGS name adds "(including the Nutrition cohort)": the CPS-II Nutrition Cohort is a subset of CPS-II "established in 1992" with over 84,000 men and 97,000 women who completed a mailed questionnaire (PMID:12015775 abstract); the genotyped colorectal sets are described only as "American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study II nested case-control study" (Supplemental table 1 of PMC11112268), not as the Nutrition Cohort; a curator may mint it later as isSubCohortOf COHO:0000024, but the tag does not distinguish it. Curator may consider relabelling COHO:0000024 to "Cancer Prevention Study II" since CPS-I and CPS-3 are distinct cohorts. 35 GWAS Catalog studies over 8 PMIDs, all GECCO colorectal or bladder cancer consortium analyses (PMID:37210288, bladder). No clash (CPS is only on COHO:0000024; KCPS is the Korean Cancer Prevention Study, tier-B row KCPS, a different string). Membership of COHO:0000020 BCAC is already recorded (aggregation_members_evidence.tsv); parent here is the new GECCO row (end of this batch), quote from the GECCO member list on the Fred Hutch page."

label: All of Us Research Program
note: GWAS-only tag, already an acronym synonym of COHO:0000423 All of Us Research Program (review row AllofUs; coho-edit.owl grep 2026-09-23). Tag AoU: 35 GWAS Catalog studies over 3 PMIDs (41882355 x20, 40902600 x13, 40823170 x2); the abstracts of PMID:41882355 and PMID:40902600 (Europe PMC, fetched 2026-09-23) name "All of Us" and "the All of Us Research Program". label: Estonian Biobank
example title: Leveraging Northern European population history: novel low-frequency variants for polycystic ovary syndrome.
example quote: For validation, we used an independent dataset from the Estonian Biobank, including 2812 cases and 89 230 controls.
note: GWAS-only tag: 61 studies, 3 PMIDs. PMID:34791234 (PCOS, 2 GCSTs, tagged FINNGEN + Estonia) validates in 'an independent dataset from the Estonian Biobank' and abbreviates it EstBB ('76% for EstBB', abstract); PMID:35922517 (COVID-19 HGI update, 5 GCSTs) lists the Estonian Biobank analysis and data collection teams among its contributors (full text PMC9352569, e.g. 'Estonian Biobank analysis team lead'); PMID:32888493 (blood-cell traits, 54 GCSTs) is not OA (Europe PMC full text, PMC and Cell supplements refused), but Supplementary Table 1 of its bioRxiv preprint (doi:10.1101/2020.01.17.910497, media-2.xlsx) lists 'Estonia_chip' ('Estonia SNP Chip') and 'Estonia_WGS' ('Estonia Whole Genome Sequencing'), both population-based and referenced to PMID:28031487, whose abstract describes 'the population-based Estonian Biobank' - so the tag there also means the Estonian Biobank (two genotyping subsets). So the tag means COHO:0000064 Estonian Biobank (synonyms EB, EGCUT, 'Estonian Genome Center of the University of Tartu'; review row EGCUT). Decision: the tag is only a country name, but CLAUDE.md says every GWAS Catalog tag for a cohort is kept as an acronym however ugly, so Estonia is proposed as an acronym synonym - curator may prefer to leave a bare country name out. EstBB (verified in the PMID:34791234 abstract) also proposed. No clash: no other COHO term, review row or tier-B row uses Estonia or EstBB (COHO:0000251 Estonian Microbiome Cohort is a sub-cohort of COHO:0000064 with different names).

input name: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
label: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
example title: Genome-wide association study meta-analysis of dizygotic twinning illuminates genetic regulation of female fecundity.
example quote: The Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research (MCTFR) was supported in part by USPHS Grants from the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (AA09367 and AA11886) and the National Institute on Drug Abuse (DA05147, DA13240, and DA024417).
definition: A collection of longitudinal, community-representative twin and adoptive family studies in Minnesota, including the Minnesota Twin Registry, the Minnesota Twin Family Study, the Enrichment Study, the Adolescent Brain study and the Sibling Interaction and Behavior Study, focusing on psychological adjustment, personality, cognitive ability and brain function with an emphasis on substance use and related psychopathology.
location quote: Lykken and his colleagues developed protocols that allowed for the successful ascertainment of large, representative samples of twins from birth records, which can be accessed for research purposes in Minnesota State.
note: 34 GWAS Catalog studies over 6 PMIDs (PMID:25387710 x17 whole-genome sequencing of psychophysiological endophenotypes, PMID:36477530 x8, PMID:39875632 x5, PMID:40962958 x2, PMID:36376304, PMID:38052102). Typed as an aggregation because the 2019 overview says the MCTFR 'comprises multiple longitudinal, community-representative investigations of twin and adoptive families' (PMID:31796137 abstract) and 'now includes five established twin cohorts and one adoption cohort' (BioC text of PMC7056536); its GWAS sample (8,405 genotyped participants clustered in four-member families, PMID:23363460) pools member studies. Members (MTR, MTFS, ES, AdBrain, SIBS) are not in COHO; the same overview lists the ABCD study (row ABCD) among new MCTFR investigations. No COHO or review-file match for MCTFR/Minnesota (grep 2026-09-23). Location quote names Minnesota only (country inferred); from the NCBI BioC text of the author manuscript PMC7056536. Example quote from the PMC10767824 acknowledgements (dizygotic twinning GWAS); the WGS paper PMID:25387710 is not open access.

input name: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease
label: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease

note: 34 GWAS Catalog studies over 3 PMIDs (32917775x24, 37291194x8, 34059833x2). No match for risc, egir or 'insulin sensitivity' in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt or the review file. Label is the PGS name, which matches the design paper (Hills et al. 2004, PMID:14968294: 'The RISC (Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease) Study'); the paper title calls it the EGIR-RISC Study (European group for the study of insulin resistance), so EGIR-RISC is added as acronym. Example quote from the full text of PMID:37291194 (insulin-stimulated glucose uptake GWAS, PMC7614755), which also points to http://www.egir.org/egirrisc/ (not fetched). Definition from the PMID:14968294 abstract and PMC2709880 (PMID:19455304). Left unlocated: the sources only count the countries without naming them (PMID:14968294 abstract: 'to study insulin resistance and CVD risk in 1500 healthy people aged 30 to 60 years from 20 centres in 13 countries'; PMC2709880: 'healthy men and women of European ancestry, aged between 30 and 60 years, were recruited from 19 centres in 14 European countries').

example quote: We used data from the Rotterdam Study (RSI, RSII and RSIII) to create three hand OA phenotypes

location quote: The first cohort (RS-I) started in 1990 and included 7,983 inhabitants, aged ≥55 years from Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
parent quote: The Rotterdam Study (RS) is a prospective, population-based cohort study of determinants of chronic diseases in older adults (7). The first cohort (RS-I) started in 1990 and included 7,983 inhabitants, aged ≥55 years from Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
note: GWAS-only tag, no PGS row. 34 GWAS Catalog studies over 4 PMIDs (32888493x24, 33510174x6, 33055079x3, 33717105x1). RSI is the first cohort (RS-I) of the Rotterdam Study (COHO:0000148, whose only synonym is RS): PMID:33055079 (abstract) and PMID:33717105 (PMC7944992, which spells it RS-I) say so explicitly; in PMID:33510174 (muscle weakness, PMC7844411) the main text names only Rotterdam affiliations, and PMID:32888493 (blood-cell traits) is not open access and its PMC BioC text does not contain RSI, so those two are assumed to be the same Rotterdam sub-cohort (co-tagged with Airwave and InCHIANTI; a curator may check their supplements). No match for RSI or RS-I in coho-edit.owl, coho_list.txt, the review file or the tier-B list. Label 'Rotterdam Study I' follows usage such as 'the Rotterdam Study I–IV' (PMC12481288); the tag RSI and the spelling RS-I are acronyms. The GWAS Catalog also tags 6 studies RSII (the second cohort, not in the tier-B list); RS-III is a third. Example quote from the PMID:33055079 abstract (hand osteoarthritis GWAS, GCST90010716); definition, location and parent quotes from PMC7944992 (PMID:33717105).

input name: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
label: Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
other synonyms: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
example title: Genome-wide association analysis identifies ancestry-specific genetic variation associated with acute response to metformin and glipizide in SUGAR-MGH.
example quote: The Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans (SUGAR-MGH) examined the acute response to metformin and glipizide in order to identify new pharmacogenetic associations for the response to common glucose-lowering medications in individuals at risk of type 2 diabetes.
definition: A pharmacogenetic study established in 2007 at Massachusetts General Hospital, which from 2008 enrolled about 1,000 adults of diverse ancestry enriched for risk of type 2 diabetes and challenged them with glipizide and metformin at clinical research centres in Boston, Massachusetts, to identify genetic variants influencing the acute response to glucose-lowering drugs.
location quote: All CRC visits took place at an academic medical center (Massachusetts General Hospital, Brigham and Women’s Hospital, or the Joslin Diabetes Center, all in Boston, MA).
note: 33 GWAS Catalog studies, all from PMID:37233759 (the SUGAR-MGH GWAS; its Europe PMC full text PMC10790310 returned HTTP 500, so example quote is from the abstract). No match in COHO (coho_list.txt, coho-edit.owl and components grep for SUGAR, Metformin 2026-09-23) or the review file; no acronym clash. Label drops the leading 'The' of the PGS name (kept as other synonym). Definition from the design paper PMC4374872 (PMID:25812009, ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01762046: established 2007, first participant enrolled 14 February 2008, planned 1,000 participants 'enriched for individuals at risk of requiring anti-diabetic therapy in the future', recruitment of non-White groups, visits at MGH, Brigham and Women's and Joslin clinical research centres) and the PMID:37233759 abstract ('One thousand participants at risk for type 2 diabetes from diverse ancestries underwent sequential glipizide and metformin challenges'). Location quote names Boston, MA, not the country. Not a sub-cohort of the Mass General Brigham Biobank (COHO:0000383): a separately recruited study.

label: Colon Cancer Family Registry
other synonyms: Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort
example title: Genome-wide association studies and Mendelian randomization analyses provide insights into the causes of early-onset colorectal cancer.
example quote: We conducted a GWAS meta-analysis of 6176 EOCRC cases and 65 829 controls from the Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium (GECCO), the Colorectal Transdisciplinary Study (CORECT), the Colon Cancer Family Registry (CCFR), and the UK Biobank.
definition: An international registry and cohort, funded by the US National Cancer Institute and begun in 1997, of colorectal cancer cases, their unaffected relatives and population-based controls recruited through six centres in Australasia and North America (the Australasian, Mayo Clinic, Ontario, Seattle, University of Hawaii and USC Consortium registries), as a resource for research on familial and sporadic colorectal cancer.
location quote: Support for case ascertainment was provided in part from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program and the following U.S. state cancer registries: AZ, CO, MN, NC, NH; and by the Victoria Cancer Registry (Australia) and Ontario Cancer Registry (Canada).
note: 32 GWAS Catalog studies over 9 PMIDs, all pooled colorectal cancer analyses of GECCO/CORECT/CCFR (in PMID:38408508 and PMID:38809988 the tag stands beside GECCO and CORECT tags as a consortium-level label). No COHO or review-file match for CCFR / Colon Cancer Family / Colon CFR (grep 2026-09-23); no acronym clash. Typed as a cohort because its own literature calls it the "Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort" (cohort profile PMID:29490034, not open access; PMC4762074, PMC5706810); a curator may prefer an aggregation of its six site registries (e.g. the Ontario Familial Colorectal Cancer Registry, Seattle Colorectal Cancer Family Registry), which are not in COHO. No parent: the Fred Hutch GECCO page says "Additionally, the Colon Cancer Family Registry (CCFR) and the Colorectal Transdisciplinary study (CORECT) are collaborating with GECCO on many analyses", i.e. CCFR is a partner consortium, not a GECCO member. The Newfoundland registry (NFCCR, row below) is not one of the six CCFR centres named in the funding statement of PMC4762074. Definition from PMC3616155 ("a National Cancer Institute (NCI)–funded registry of CRC cases, unaffected family members, and population-based controls"; "an international collaborative study initiated in 1997") and PMC4762074 (recruitment 1997-2012 "in Australasia and North America"; the six centres). Location quote from the CCFR funding acknowledgement in PMC11112268; the Australasian registry may also have recruited in New Zealand, which I did not verify, so New Zealand is not asserted.

note: 32 GWAS Catalog studies, 1 PMID (PMID:40181193, CHARGE gene-sleep interaction meta-analysis for blood pressure; Europe PMC full text and supplementary files unavailable, so the example quote comes from Supplementary file 2 (cohort descriptions, docx) downloaded from the publisher's article page).
